housing.summary: Numbeo reported NOK 19,222.90 per month for a one-bedroom apartment in Oslo city centre, last updated 26 August 2026: https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Oslo. The City of Oslo says the usual security deposit is three months' rent, held in a regulated deposit account: https://www.oslo.kommune.no/english/welcome-to-oslo/accommodation/renting-a-home/. FINN Eiendom is a major local rental portal with an Oslo-specific listings page: https://www.finn.no/realestate/lettings/search.html?location=0.20061.

banking.summary: DNB's official newcomer guidance says a new arrival needs a D-number, valid identification and supporting documentation presented at a bank office; newcomers must identify themselves at a DNB office: https://www.dnb.no/kundeprogram/bli-kunde/ny-i-norge?la=NO.
required_docs: valid identification, such as a valid passport
supporting documentation requested by the bank

schools.summary: The City of Oslo's international-school directory identifies IB programmes and French- and German-curriculum schools in Oslo: https://www.oslo.kommune.no/english/welcome-to-oslo/children-families/primary-and-secondary-schools-in-oslo/.

legal_admin.summary: At Oslo's Service Centre for Foreign Workers, EU/EEA citizens intending to stay more than three months book a police appointment for a registration certificate: https://www.sua.no/en/book-appointment/eu-eea/. Non-EU/EEA citizens with a granted residence permit book a police appointment, appear in person, hand in documents, have a photo taken and order a residence card: https://www.sua.no/en/book-appointment/non-eu-eea/.
legal_admin.registration_step: Follow the citizenship-specific SUA route: EU/EEA citizens staying more than three months book a police appointment for a registration certificate; non-EU/EEA citizens whose permit has been granted book a police appointment and appear in person to order the residence card.

tax_finance.summary: A foreign worker needs a Norwegian identification number (D-number or national identity number) and a tax deduction card. With electronic ID, apply online; without an identification number, book an ID-check appointment and bring completed form RF-1209, or ask the employer to apply: https://www.skatteetaten.no/en/forms/tax-deduction-card-for-foreign-citizens/.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Norwegian identification number (D-number or national identity number)

transport.summary: Ruter is Oslo's public-transport network; its adult 30-day Zone 1 pass costs NOK 655 from 3 May 2026: https://ruter.no/en/nyheter/the-price-of-a-30-day-ticket-for-adults-and-children-will-be-reduced-on-may-3. EU/EEA licences can be exchanged for the corresponding Norwegian category without new tests: https://www.vegvesen.no/en/driving-licences/driving-licence-holders/foreign-driving-licence-in-norway/exchanging-eueea-driving-licences/. A non-EU/EEA licence can be exchanged only when its issuing country is listed by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration: https://www.vegvesen.no/en/driving-licences/driving-licence-holders/foreign-driving-licence-in-norway/exchange-of-driving-licences-from-countries-outside-the-eueea/. Residents registered in the National Population Register are entitled to a GP; registration and changes are managed through Helsenorge or its guidance service: https://www.helsenorge.no/en/gp/about-gp/the-right-to-a-doctor/.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences may be exchanged for the corresponding Norwegian category without new tests. Non-EU/EEA exchange is available only for issuing countries specifically listed by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration; other non-EU/EEA licences cannot be exchanged.
transport.healthcare_registration: Register as a resident in the National Population Register to become entitled to a GP, then manage GP registration through Helsenorge or its guidance service; most D-number holders are not entitled to a GP, subject to listed exceptions.
